On the right, layout_spectral() places the nodes by two eigenvectors of the graph's Laplacian, which recovers the grid: nine nodes in three rows of three, joined to their neighbors." width="100%"} The coordinates of each node are its entries in the eigenvectors of the second and third smallest eigenvalues of the Laplacian `L = D - A`. These vectors are the smoothest non-constant functions on the graph, so adjacent nodes get similar coordinates: the layout shows the global shape (rings, grids, the two halves of a barbell) cleanly, but it can crowd dense regions into a small area. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. This matches NetworkX's `spectral_layout()`, up to the sign of each axis, which is fixed here so that the first node with a nonzero coordinate has a positive one. Edge direction is ignored (directed graphs use `A + A^T`), parallel edges add up and self-loops are skipped. A disconnected graph has several zero eigenvalues, so its components collapse onto a few points; lay out components separately or use a force-directed layout instead. Graphs of 400 nodes and more use a sparse eigensolver. Graphs with one or two nodes have no third eigenvector: one node goes to `center=`, two nodes to either side of it. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use edge weights (`1` where missing) as adjacency entries. If `False`, every edge counts `1`. If `None` (default), follows whether the graph was created as weighted. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. `None` keeps the raw eigenvector entries (`center=` is then ignored). Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `weighted=True` and an edge weight is negative or not finite, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~fiedler_vector`) : Compute the Laplacian eigenvector used to split a graph. [](`~laplacian_matrix`) : Build the graph's Laplacian matrix. [](`~layout_spring`) : Place nodes with a force-directed spring model. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The positions come from eigenvectors of the graph's Laplacian, which place nodes with many edges between them close together. A grid comes out as a grid: ::: {#a90a8531 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_grid_graph([6, 6]).layout_spectral().plot(layout="pos") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Two planted groups A planted partition graph has 30 nodes in two groups of 15, with each pair in the same group joined with probability 0.4 and each pair across the groups with probability 0.03. The first coordinate of the spectral layout splits the nodes into the two groups exactly: ::: {#425c0362 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_planted_partition_graph(2, 15, 0.4, 0.03, seed=1) pos = graph.layout_spectral(return_dict=True) group = graph.get_node_attrs("community") left = {group[n] for n, (x, y) in pos.items() if x < 0} right = {group[n] for n, (x, y) in pos.items() if x > 0} left, right ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ({1}, {0}) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8a8df12d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.layout_spectral().plot( layout="pos", color_by="community", show_labels=False, height=400 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The layout needs no seed. It is quick for sparse graphs, but it can crowd nodes that the eigenvectors don't tell apart, as in the tight group on the right.
